# CLAUDE.md — profile `test-kyle`

You are looking at a Factum profile folder: the complete record of one
person's surface nerve/muscle recordings. Read this file first; it
explains the layout, the metrics, and the situation, so you can work
from the data without needing anything else.

## Who this is

Kyle, a bilateral upper-limb amputee. **The two sides are different,
and it changes what each one can do:**

- **Left — amputated about an inch above the wrist bone**, so the wrist
  bone is gone. A long transradial residual limb: nearly the whole
  forearm remains, and with it the finger and wrist muscle bellies.
  This is the working arm and the only one a forearm band fits.
- **Right — amputated at the elbow.** No forearm at all. A forearm band
  has nowhere to sit; only upper-arm muscle (biceps, triceps) remains,
  which carries no finger content. It can serve as a coarse extra
  switch, never as a second hand.

The movements recorded here are **attempted or phantom movements**, not
executed ones: there is no hand to move, and the signal comes from the
residual limb.

A helper puts the band on him, so repeatable placement is a first-class
concern rather than a detail. Placement is recorded as numbers —
millimetres from the elbow crease and degrees of rotation around the
limb — against a drawn limb in the app, written to `profile.json` and
mirrored into `placement_notes.md`. Every probe CSV carries the
placement in its header.

He cannot reliably operate a mouse or keyboard, which is why the app
that produced this data automates almost everything and asks for as
few clicks as possible. His own priority is using his iPhone; the PC
is the development platform.

`left/` and `right/` are separate sub-trees because the two limbs are
independent signal sources — but they are NOT equivalent sources. An
earlier version of this note claimed two limbs double the available
vocabulary. That was written before the amputation levels were known
and it is wrong: there is one forearm here.

## What the hardware is

A Mudra Band on the forearm: three surface electrodes sampling at
about 1000 Hz, delivered as SNC (surface nerve conduction) data over a
local WebSocket. Channel order is fixed everywhere in this project:

| Column | Electrode |
|--------|-----------|
| `ch1`  | ulnar     |
| `ch2`  | median    |
| `ch3`  | radial    |

Values are raw, in the range -1..+1, exactly as the Mudra host
delivered them. **No filtering is applied on write** — every probe CSV
says `filters: none`. If a recording is filtered in future, that
header field is where it will say so.

The band's stock gestures (tap, pinch, swipe, point, rotate) are all
defined by fingers touching or a hand rotating, and its pressure
feature measures literal thumb-to-finger contact. None of that is
anatomically available here. That is why everything in this folder is
his own signal, discovered from scratch — **there is no fixed movement
list anywhere in this project.**

## Folder layout

```
test-kyle/
    profile.json          name, type, notes, active arm, open sessions
    CLAUDE.md             this file
    README.md             the same thing for a human reader
    placement/            photos and marks for repeatable band placement
    left/  right/         one sub-tree per arm — they are independent
        placement_notes.md    timestamped log of where the band sat
        sessions/
            2026-08-14_1430/          one visit, one arm
                session.json          date, location, who was present,
                                      notes, battery %, charger y/n
                session_notes.md      free-text running log, timestamped
                probes/
                    001_rest_1430.csv
                    002_curl-ring-finger_1433.csv
                probes.json           manifest: metadata + metrics for
                                      every probe in the session
                analysis.json         full analysis, machine-readable
                REPORT.md             the same analysis, for humans
                ANALYSIS_PROMPT.md    ready-made prompt for this session
```

Sessions are **append-only**. A session folder is never overwritten and
never renamed, because comparing the same movement across days is how
we detect drift in placement, skin condition and fatigue.

## What a probe is

One short recording of one attempted movement, named by him in his own
words ("curl ring finger", "the twitchy one"). Default 30 seconds.
Each file opens with a self-describing comment header:

```
# profile: test-kyle
# arm: left
# session: 2026-08-14_1430
# probe: curl ring finger
# started: 2026-08-14T14:33:07
# duration_s: 30
# sample_rate_hz: 1000
# effort: moderate
# fatigue: some
# his_confidence: 4
# placement: 3 fingers below elbow crease, ulnar side, mark A
# filters: none
# notes: felt distinct to him
timestamp,ch1,ch2,ch3
```

`timestamp` is milliseconds since the start of that probe.
`status: incomplete` in a header means the recording was interrupted —
the data before that point is still valid and still worth using.

Every session starts with a **rest** probe. Baseline drifts with
placement, skin and fatigue, so every other measurement in a session is
relative to that session's own rest recording. A comparison against a
different day's baseline is meaningless.

## The metrics

- **snr_vs_rest** — How much louder the channel is than this session's rest recording, in dB. 0 dB means indistinguishable from rest. Above ~6 dB is a signal you can see; above ~12 dB is comfortable.
- **onset_latency_s** — Seconds from the start of the recording to the first burst of activity. Only meaningful when he was cued to start immediately.
- **rise_time_s** — How long the first burst took to go from 10% to 90% of its peak. Shorter is a crisper onset and easier to trigger on.
- **reps** — Bursts of activity found in the recording — one per attempt at the movement.
- **consistency** — How alike the repetitions are, 0-1, computed as 1/(1 + mean coefficient of variation of the feature vector across repetitions). 1.0 means identical every time. This is the number that matters most: a movement he cannot repeat identically is unusable no matter how strong it is. Above 0.70 is good, below 0.50 is a problem.
- **channel_signature** — Share of the movement's energy carried by each electrode. A movement concentrated on one channel is easier to separate than one spread evenly across all three.
- **usability** — Overall 0-1 score, weighted heavily toward whether the movement repeats reliably. Effort and fatigue are recorded but carry little weight: a tiring movement that gives a good, repeatable result is worth keeping. See 'How usability is scored'.
- **d_prime** — Separability between two probes along the best linear boundary. Below 1.0 the classifier will confuse them; above 1.5 they are usably distinct; above 3.0 they are unmistakable.

Scoring: usability = 0.45 x consistency + 0.25 x strength + 0.20 x his confidence + 0.10 x effort, minus a small fatigue tie-breaker (none 0, some 0.02, high 0.05). Consistency is weighted highest on purpose: a movement he cannot repeat identically is unusable no matter how strong it is. Effort and fatigue are recorded and reported but deliberately carry little weight — a movement that produces a good, repeatable result is worth keeping even if it is tiring, and should not be scored out of contention for it.

## Ground rules of this project

- **CSV and JSON only** for data. No pickle, no npz. A fitted
  classifier `.pkl` is acceptable but must always be shadowed by a JSON
  metrics file beside it.
- **Everything lives under a profile.** Nothing is written outside a
  profile folder.
- **Consistency and low effort beat raw signal strength.** A weak
  movement performed identically every time is more useful than a
  strong one that varies. A movement that tires him will not survive
  daily use, however good its numbers look.
- **The goal is the smallest set of reliably separable signals**, not
  the largest.
- Raw sample arrays are never sent to an API. Work from `probes.json`,
  `analysis.json` and `REPORT.md`; open a CSV only when you need a
  specific number from it.

## If you are asked to analyse a session

Start with that session's `REPORT.md`, then `analysis.json` for the
numbers behind it, then `probes.json` for per-probe metadata. Each
session also has an `ANALYSIS_PROMPT.md` written for exactly this
purpose. Useful questions to answer: which probes should be promoted
into a training set, which pairs will be confused, what changed since
the last session, and what specifically to try next.
